project.title: Retail order integration
project.description: Reference production design for accepting customer and partner orders, committing them atomically, and publishing an idempotent fulfillment event.

requirements.text: Customers and approved partners can submit an order exactly once from the caller perspective.
requirements.acceptance: A valid request returns an order ID and duplicate idempotency keys return the original result.

requirements.text: The production order submission path meets 99.9% monthly availability.
requirements.acceptance: Monthly SLI calculated at the edge is at least 99.9%, excluding approved maintenance.

requirements.text: Order data recovery meets RPO 15 minutes and RTO 60 minutes.
requirements.acceptance: A quarterly restore exercise recovers the service within 60 minutes with no more than 15 minutes of committed order loss.

evidence.note: Reference recovery objective pending operational approval.

requirements.text: Order submission completes within 800 ms at p95 under the approved peak load.
requirements.acceptance: A production-like load test demonstrates p95 under 800 ms with error rate below 0.5%.

evidence.note: Reference latency target for the example.

requirements.text: All public and workload access is authenticated, least privilege, encrypted, logged, and protected from common web abuse.
requirements.acceptance: Threat review and policy evidence show WAF, mTLS or OIDC, workload identity, private data access, encryption, and audit logging.

evidence.note: Reference security gate for the example.

requirements.text: Order and customer data remains in approved US regions with seven-year order retention and audited access.
requirements.acceptance: Region, retention, deletion, backup, and access-log controls are configured and evidenced.

evidence.note: Reference data-governance rule for the example.

requirements.text: The service has reproducible delivery, end-to-end telemetry, actionable alerts, runbooks, and tested rollback and restore.
requirements.acceptance: Release and game-day evidence shows health verification, rollback, alert ownership, runbooks, and restore success.

evidence.note: Reference operational gate for the example.

requirements.text: The workload has cost ownership, budgets, anomaly alerts, and quarterly right-sizing review.
requirements.acceptance: Budget and anomaly alerts are active and a quarterly unit-cost review is scheduled.

evidence.note: Reference FinOps requirement for the example.

requirements.text: Customers can review and submit an order through a responsive, accessible, retry-safe web experience.
requirements.acceptance: Compact and wide layouts cover default, loading, empty, error, success, permission-denied, and offline behavior; keyboard and screen-reader tests pass WCAG 2.2 AA acceptance criteria; duplicate submission is prevented with the same idempotency key.

evidence.note: Reference UI implementation and acceptance contract.

controls.name: Edge protection
controls.description: Protect public order entry points and restrict origin access.
controls.implementation: Front Door Premium WAF, bot and rate rules, DDoS decision, TLS policy, and private APIM origin.

controls.name: Workload identity and secrets
controls.description: Remove embedded credentials and scope Azure access to individual workloads.
controls.implementation: Entra Workload ID, managed identities, Key Vault CSI, least-privilege RBAC, rotation, and access logging.

controls.name: Private data plane
controls.description: Keep confidential stores and messaging off the public internet.
controls.implementation: Private endpoints, Private DNS, firewall egress, encryption, database RBAC, and audited access.

controls.name: Atomic outbox
controls.description: Prevent an accepted order from being lost between database commit and event publication.
controls.implementation: Order and outbox row commit in one PostgreSQL transaction; worker publishes idempotently and records completion.

controls.name: End-to-end observability
controls.description: Correlate customer outcome, service behavior, dependency health, and event delivery.
controls.implementation: OpenTelemetry correlation, structured logs, managed Prometheus, Application Insights, SLO dashboards, alerts, and runbooks.

controls.name: Restricted AKS workload baseline
controls.description: Enforce production-safe workload, network, and disruption defaults.
controls.implementation: Restricted PSS, non-root, seccomp, no privilege escalation, dropped capabilities, requests/limits, probes, PDB, topology spread, HPA, and default-deny policy.

controls.name: Software supply-chain integrity
controls.description: Promote only reviewed, scanned, signed, immutable artifacts.
controls.implementation: Dependency and secret scan, image scan, SBOM, signed provenance, digest promotion, admission verification, and health-gated GitOps rollout.

controls.name: Tested backup and restore
controls.description: Recover order state and platform configuration within the agreed objectives.
controls.implementation: PostgreSQL PITR, immutable backup protection, GitOps bootstrap, quarterly restore exercise, and measured RTO/RPO evidence.

controls.name: FinOps guardrails
controls.description: Make workload cost visible and owned.
controls.implementation: Required tags, budgets, anomaly alerts, autoscaling bounds, log-retention limits, and quarterly cost-per-order review.

personas.name: Authenticated retail customer
goals: Recover safely from a transient failure
access_needs: Clear error recovery without relying on color

flows.name: Review and submit an order
flows.goal: Submit one valid order and receive a durable confirmation without duplicate creation.
preconditions: Cart has at least one available item
A stable checkout idempotency key exists

steps.action: reviews items, quantities, totals, and delivery information
steps.outcome: The complete order summary and editable fields are available in logical reading order.
steps.alternate: Unavailable items are identified inline and submission remains disabled until resolved.

steps.outcome: The action is disabled, the same idempotency key is sent, progress is announced, and duplicate activation is prevented.
steps.alternate: A network or service error preserves entered data and offers a retry with the same key.

steps.outcome: A durable confirmation, next step, and navigation to orders are available and announced.

outcomes: The customer receives an order ID
Submission status is understandable without motion or color alone
exceptions: Backend rejection with retry-safe correlation ID

screens.name: Review and submit order
screens.purpose: Let an authenticated customer verify the order, correct issues, submit once, and recover without losing work.

states.name: Ready to review
states.trigger: Order data and authorization are available
states.content: Review order details and submit when the summary is correct.
states.focus_target: Page heading on initial navigation; preserve current focus after inline edits

states.name: Loading order
states.trigger: Order query is pending with no usable cached result
states.content: Loading the order summary; controls are not exposed until labels and values are available.
states.focus_target: Keep focus on the initiating navigation target

states.name: Empty cart
states.trigger: The order contains no purchasable items
states.content: Your cart is empty. Add an item before checkout.

states.name: Submission failed safely
states.trigger: Validation, timeout, or service failure prevents confirmed submission
states.content: The order was not confirmed. Your information is preserved; retry uses the same checkout key.
states.focus_target: Error summary linked to affected fields
states.announcement: Order was not submitted; review the error and retry

states.name: Order confirmed
states.trigger: The API returns the durable order ID
states.content: Order confirmed. The order ID and next fulfillment step are available.

states.name: Permission denied
states.trigger: The session is missing, expired, or lacks the customer role
states.content: Sign in again to review this order. No order details are disclosed.
states.announcement: You are not authorized to review this order

states.name: Offline
states.content: You appear to be offline. Your entered information remains local to this checkout session.
states.announcement: Offline; order has not been submitted

components.name: Checkout page header
components.description: Semantic banner with page title, progress context, and route actions.
components.accessibility: Uses banner landmark, one h1, descriptive link name, and logical focus order.
components.implementation: Reuse the product page-header primitive; do not create a checkout-only navigation system.

components.name: Order summary
components.description: Responsive summary of items, price, fulfillment, and masked customer details.
components.accessibility: Uses headings and lists or table semantics appropriate to content; totals do not rely on visual position alone.
components.implementation: Pure presentation component with typed props and component-level accessibility tests.

components.name: Order review form
components.description: Validated delivery fields, error summary, terms control, and retry-safe submit action.
components.accessibility: Native labels and controls, programmatic error association, error summary links, described requirements, and no focus loss during validation.
components.implementation: Use repository-native schema validation and form primitives; keep idempotency key outside editable controls.

components.name: Order status panel
components.description: Contextual progress, error, offline, permission, and confirmation message with recovery actions.
components.accessibility: Uses status or alert semantics intentionally, avoids duplicate announcements, moves focus only when task context changes, and never relies on color alone.
components.implementation: Reuse the product message-bar/status primitive with an owned live-region policy.

bindings.operation: Create order using the approved order API contract
bindings.transport: HTTPS/443 with OIDC access token and Idempotency-Key
bindings.request: Validated order draft, delivery selection, terms acknowledgement, correlation ID, and stable idempotency key; no secrets or analytics payload.
bindings.response: Confirmed order ID and status, or a typed validation/auth/transient/permanent error with safe customer message and correlation ID.
bindings.authorization: Customer role and resource ownership validated at the API; the UI check is convenience, not the security boundary.
bindings.loading: Disable repeat submit, preserve all data, expose busy state, and announce progress without animation.
bindings.error: Map typed errors to field summary or status panel; retain the same idempotency key for safe retry; never imply success without an order ID.

navigation.trigger: Open a saved checkout deep link or return from the order list
navigation.condition: Checkout exists and is still editable
navigation.guard: Require customer role; prompt before abandoning dirty unsaved edits
navigation.back_behavior: Browser Back returns to the prior safe route without resubmitting; refresh rehydrates by checkout ID and retains the idempotency key

accessibility.keyboard: All controls use native keyboard behavior; reading and focus order follows region order; no keyboard trap; retry and error-summary links are reachable.
accessibility.focus: Set focus to the page heading on navigation, error summary on blocking validation, and confirmation heading after durable success; restore focus to the triggering action when a transient panel closes.
accessibility.screen_reader: Use semantic landmarks/headings/forms, programmatic labels and errors, page titles, status announcements, and non-color state names; avoid duplicate live-region messages.
accessibility.contrast: Semantic tokens must pass text and non-text contrast in default, hover, focus, disabled, error, and high-contrast states.
accessibility.zoom_reflow: At 200% zoom and 320 CSS pixels, regions reflow to the compact layout without horizontal page scrolling or loss of content/actions.
accessibility.reduced_motion: No animation or auto-advancing content is permitted; state changes are immediate, labeled, and announced when appropriate.
testing: Automated axe-core checks in component and E2E CI
Manual keyboard-only journey at compact and wide breakpoints
Manual screen reader journey with NVDA and VoiceOver
Contrast, high-contrast, 200% zoom, 320 CSS-pixel reflow, and text-spacing checks

implementation.front_end: Reuse the existing web application stack; for this standalone reference use React plus TypeScript as a proposed example, not a repository fact.
implementation.design_system_package: Use the repository package when present; otherwise adopt Fluent UI React v9 behind product-owned wrapper components.
implementation.state_management: Keep ephemeral form state local; represent server state with typed query keys and an explicit submission state machine.
implementation.data_fetching: Typed API client with OIDC token injection, correlation ID, bounded timeout, cancellation, and no automatic unsafe POST retry.
implementation.validation: Shared schema contract for client guidance plus authoritative server validation; map typed errors to fields and the error summary.
implementation.testing: Unit tests for state reducers and mapping, component tests for semantics/states, contract tests for API types, E2E success/error/offline/permission journeys, accessibility checks, and visual regression at both breakpoints.
implementation.feature_flags: Release behind an owned checkout-review flag with explicit default, audience, expiry, kill switch, and telemetry.
implementation.observability: Capture Web Vitals, route and submit latency, typed failure class, retry and abandonment counts, and correlation ID; redact order/customer content and tokens.

analytics.trigger: After a durable success or typed terminal failure
analytics.privacy: No order ID, customer ID, item data, free text, token, address, or correlation ID is emitted; follow consent and bounded retention policy.

decisions.title: Use the existing enterprise AKS platform
decisions.context: The organization already operates an AKS application platform and adjacent retail services share its policy, GitOps, and support model.
decisions.choice: Deploy the order API and outbox worker into a private AKS cluster under an owned production namespace.
decisions.rationale: Reuses established platform capability and avoids a second operating model for the same team.
consequences: Platform team remains accountable for cluster lifecycle.
Application team must meet the restricted workload baseline.
A simpler managed runtime should be reconsidered if platform reuse is no longer true.

decisions.title: Use a transactional outbox for event publication
decisions.context: Order acceptance and event publication must not diverge, and distributed transactions are not supported across PostgreSQL and Service Bus.
decisions.choice: Commit the order and outbox row in one transaction, then publish asynchronously with a stable event ID.
decisions.rationale: Avoids dual-write loss while preserving durable retry and independent fulfillment processing.
consequences: The worker and outbox backlog require operational ownership.
Consumers must be idempotent.
Event publication is eventually consistent after order acceptance.

decisions.title: Use Service Bus Premium for the order event
decisions.context: The integration needs durable delivery, bounded redelivery, dead-lettering, private connectivity, and enterprise ownership.
decisions.choice: Publish OrderCreated v2 to a Service Bus Premium topic with an owned fulfillment subscription and DLQ.
decisions.rationale: Meets the enterprise integration requirement without operating a broker on AKS.
consequences: Throughput and messaging-unit capacity must be load tested.
Replay and DLQ runbooks are required.
Event contract versioning is part of the implementation.

decisions.title: Keep confidential PaaS services private
decisions.context: Order data is confidential and public data-plane exposure is unnecessary.
decisions.choice: Use private endpoints, Private DNS, and controlled egress for PostgreSQL, Service Bus, Key Vault, and ACR.
decisions.rationale: Reduces exposure and aligns with the application landing-zone network model.
consequences: DNS and network dependencies become production-critical.
Platform team owns endpoint, route, and firewall lifecycle.
Troubleshooting requires cross-team telemetry.

decisions.title: Use federated workload identity
decisions.context: Long-lived credentials in workload configuration create rotation and compromise risk.
decisions.choice: Use Entra Workload ID and managed identities for Azure resource access.
decisions.rationale: Provides short-lived tokens, per-workload scope, and auditable access without stored cloud credentials.
consequences: Federated credentials and service accounts must be managed as code.
Each workload needs explicit least-privilege role assignments.

decisions.title: Use one region with zonal high availability for initial production
decisions.context: The assumed 99.9% SLO and 60-minute RTO do not currently justify active multi-region complexity.
decisions.choice: Use zone-aware AKS, API Management capacity, PostgreSQL HA, and Service Bus Premium in East US 2 with tested restore.
decisions.rationale: Meets the assumed objectives with lower operational and data-consistency complexity.
consequences: A regional outage can exceed the monthly SLO and requires restore or redeployment.
Business must confirm the SLO and RTO assumption before approval.
A second region should be added if objectives tighten.

decisions.title: Promote signed digests through GitOps
decisions.context: Production deployment needs immutable artifacts, peer-reviewed desired state, provenance, and deterministic rollback.
decisions.choice: Build once, scan and sign the image, promote its digest through protected environment repositories, and let Flux reconcile it.
decisions.rationale: Separates artifact production from environment approval and provides an auditable desired state.
consequences: Signing and admission availability are deployment dependencies.
Emergency change has a documented and audited Git path.
Rollback is a Git revision and prior signed digest.

decisions.title: Measure SLOs at the customer edge and correlate dependencies
decisions.context: Platform health alone does not show whether customers can place orders.
decisions.choice: Calculate availability and latency SLIs at Front Door and correlate them with APIM, AKS, PostgreSQL, Service Bus, and business-event telemetry.
decisions.rationale: Connects alerts and error budgets to the user outcome while retaining dependency diagnosis.
consequences: Telemetry requires redaction and bounded retention.
SRE and product owners share SLO governance.
Exporter failure must not block order processing.

risks.title: Automated abuse or volumetric traffic reaches the order API
risks.mitigation: Front Door Premium WAF, bot and rate rules, DDoS decision, authentication, origin restriction, load shedding, and alerting.

risks.title: A shared or long-lived credential grants excessive Azure access
risks.mitigation: Workload identity, per-service accounts, least-privilege roles, Key Vault, PIM, rotation, and access review.

risks.title: Confidential order data is exposed through a public or over-permissive data path
risks.mitigation: Private endpoints, Private DNS, encryption, scoped identities, audited access, classification, retention, and policy controls.

risks.title: An accepted order is never published for fulfillment
risks.mitigation: Atomic outbox, backlog-age alert, durable retry, reconciliation, and owned recovery runbook.

risks.title: A retried event causes duplicate fulfillment action
risks.mitigation: Stable event ID, idempotent consumer record, bounded redelivery, and audited replay.

risks.title: Order-path degradation is not detected before material customer impact
risks.mitigation: Edge SLIs, dependency and business telemetry, error-budget alerts, synthetic checks, owned runbooks, and game days.

risks.title: An AKS workload bypasses isolation or production safety defaults
risks.mitigation: Restricted PSS, admission policy, default-deny network policy, non-root baseline, quotas, GitOps, and policy evidence.

risks.title: A vulnerable or untrusted artifact reaches production
risks.mitigation: Protected source, scanning, SBOM, signed provenance, digest promotion, admission verification, and rollback.

risks.title: A regional outage exceeds the assumed availability objective
risks.mitigation: Zonal HA, tested restore and GitOps bootstrap, recovery runbook, business acceptance of the regional tradeoff, and a trigger for multi-region reassessment.

assumptions.text: A supported enterprise AKS platform and skilled operating team already exist.
assumptions.consequence: If false, Container Apps or App Service should be reconsidered before implementation.

assumptions.text: 99.9% monthly availability, 60-minute RTO, and 15-minute RPO are acceptable business objectives.
assumptions.consequence: Tighter objectives can require multi-region application and data design.

assumptions.text: Service Bus Premium and the selected PostgreSQL tier can be sized after a production-like load test.
assumptions.consequence: Final SKUs and cost cannot be approved until capacity evidence exists.

open_questions.question: What are the approved peak requests per second, event rate, and payload-size distributions?
open_questions.consequence: Final APIM, PostgreSQL, Service Bus, and AKS capacity and cost remain provisional.

open_questions.question: Does the partner require public mTLS or private cross-tenant connectivity?
open_questions.consequence: The partner ingress implementation may change while the API contract remains stable.
